Grand Canyon Tour from Scottsdale: The Complete Day Trip Guide

Yes, you can see the Grand Canyon from Scottsdale in one day. The South Rim is a long run each way, so plan on 14 to 16 hours door to door. In our 14-seat Executive Sprinter a 14-hour day bills 12 hours at $145 per hour, or $1,740, about $124 per person for a full van. Everyone else sleeps on the way home. This is the planning guide; the private Grand Canyon South Rim tour is the page to book it on.

The Grand Canyon is not just a bucket-list stop. It is a humbling reminder of nature's power and time's passage, and it is a day trip away. This guide covers how to do it right.

South Rim vs. West Rim: Which Grand Canyon?

Grand Canyon South Rim (National Park)

Distance from Scottsdale: about 230 miles
Best for: first-time visitors, photographers, hikers, the iconic experience

  • Classic, famous canyon views
  • Multiple viewpoints along the Rim Trail
  • Hiking access on Bright Angel and South Kaibab
  • Visitor center, museums, historic lodges
  • Greater depth and width of canyon views

There is a per-vehicle park entrance fee at the gate.

Grand Canyon West Rim (Hualapai Tribal Land)

Distance from Scottsdale: about 250 miles
Best for: the Skywalk, helicopter tours, a shorter visit

  • Glass Skywalk extending over the canyon
  • Helicopter and boat tours available
  • Eagle Point and Guano Point views
  • Less crowded than the South Rim

Admission is per person, priced by the Hualapai Tribe, with the Skywalk as an add-on.

Our Recommendation

First-time visitors: South Rim. It is the Grand Canyon everyone pictures.
Skywalk bucket list: West Rim, if walking on glass over the canyon is the goal.
Limited time: West Rim. Slightly less hiking-focused.

The South Rim Day Trip Itinerary

The Full Day

4:30 AM - Depart Scottsdale
Yes, it is early. Coffee and breakfast en route.

5:00 AM - Quick Stop in Anthem
Coffee, breakfast sandwiches, last bathroom break before the highway.

8:30 AM - Arrive Grand Canyon Village
Beat the crowds and catch the morning light on the rim.

8:45 AM - Mather Point
The iconic overlook. Allow 30-45 minutes for photos and the "wow" moment.

9:30 AM - Rim Trail to Yavapai Point
An easy 0.7-mile paved walk. The Yavapai Geology Museum explains how the canyon formed.

10:30 AM - Bright Angel Trailhead
Walk the first half mile below the rim for a taste, and turn back whenever you like.

12:00 PM - Lunch
El Tovar Dining Room (reserve ahead), the Arizona Room for steaks with rim views, Bright Angel Lodge for casual and quick, or pack a picnic.

1:30 PM - Desert View Drive (East)
A 25-mile scenic drive with overlooks at Grandview Point, Moran Point, Lipan Point, Navajo Point, and the Desert View Watchtower.

3:45 PM - Desert View Watchtower
Climb the tower for 360-degree views and browse the Native American art.

4:30 PM - Begin the Return

8:30 PM - Arrive Scottsdale

That is a 16-hour day. Book it privately and you pay for 13 hours, because 15 or more hours earns 3 free hours.

The Shorter Itinerary (Less Driving)

6:00 AM - Depart Scottsdale
10:00 AM - Arrive South Rim
10:00 AM-4:00 PM - Grand Canyon Village: Mather Point, Rim Trail, Bright Angel Lodge; skip Desert View Drive
4:00 PM - Depart
8:00 PM - Arrive Scottsdale

Fourteen hours, billed as 12.

The West Rim Day Trip Itinerary

5:00 AM - Depart Scottsdale via US-93 through Wickenburg toward Kingman
7:00 AM - Breakfast in Wickenburg
9:00 AM - Arrive Grand Canyon West and check in
9:30 AM - Eagle Point and Skywalk: the glass horseshoe extends 70 feet over the canyon (no personal cameras on the walk)
11:00 AM - Guano Point: rugged overlook with a mining history and great photos
12:30 PM - Hualapai Ranch: quick lunch and optional horseback rides
1:30 PM - Optional add-ons: helicopter into the canyon, pontoon ride on the Colorado, zip line
3:00 PM - Depart
7:00 PM - Arrive Scottsdale

Fourteen hours, billed as 12.

Why Private Transportation for the Grand Canyon?

The Driving Challenge

  • 8 or more hours of total driving
  • Winding mountain roads and elk on the shoulder after dark
  • Weather that changes with altitude
  • Fatigue setting in on the return

What a Chauffeur Changes

  • Someone else handles the driving
  • Rest both ways: sleep, read, or work
  • No navigation stress
  • Local knowledge: the best stops, bathroom breaks, and photo pull-offs
  • Flexibility: want to stay for sunset? Say so.
  • Safety: drowsy driving after a long day is the real risk

What to Bring

Essentials (Year-Round)

  • Layers: the rim is 15-25 degrees cooler than Phoenix
  • Comfortable shoes: you will walk 3-5 miles
  • Sunscreen, sunglasses, hat: high altitude means stronger sun
  • Water: 2 liters per person
  • Camera with a spare battery: cold drains them faster
  • Snacks: options on the rim are limited

Winter Additions (November-March)

  • Heavy jacket, gloves, warm hat
  • Ice cleats for icy trails
  • Thermos with something hot

Summer Additions (June-August)

  • Extra water and electrolytes
  • Umbrella for afternoon monsoons

Best Time to Visit

Spring (March-May): mild rim temperatures, wildflowers, moderate crowds, occasional late snow
Summer (June-August): warm days, afternoon storms, longest daylight, peak crowds
Fall (September-November): ideal weather, golden aspens, fewer crowds; the best overall
Winter (December-February): cold, possible snow (stunning photos), fewest crowds, some reduced services

Weekdays are noticeably quieter than weekends, and holidays are packed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Grand Canyon worth a day trip from Scottsdale?
Absolutely. It is a long day, but one view from the rim makes it worthwhile.

Can we actually see the canyon in one day?
You will walk the rim, see multiple viewpoints, and understand why it is a wonder of the world. You will not hike to the bottom; that is a multi-day permit trip.

How many hours should we book?
Fourteen for the shorter South Rim or West Rim day, sixteen for the full Desert View Drive itinerary. The free-hour rule means you pay for 12 or 13.

What if the weather is bad?
Canyon weather is local. Phoenix can be cloudy while the rim is clear. Check the rim webcams before you leave.

Is it safe to hike into the canyon on a day trip?
The first mile or two of Bright Angel Trail is safe and rewarding. Do not attempt the river and back in one day.
